title.zh: 卷七十七 列傳第七: 耶律屋質 耶律吼 耶律安摶 耶律洼 耶律頹昱 耶律撻烈
title.en: Volume 77 Biographies 7: Yelu Wuzhi, Yelu Hou, Yelu Antuan, Yelu Wa, Yelu Tuiyu, Yelu Talie
title.raw: 卷七十七 列傳第七: 耶律屋質 耶律吼 耶律安摶 耶律洼 耶律頹昱 耶律撻烈 Volume 77 Biographies 7: Yelu Wuzhi, Yelu Hou, Yelu Antuan, Yelu Wa, Yelu Tuiyu, Yelu Talie

sentences.zh: 耶律屋質耶律吼

translations.literal: Yelü Wuzhi, Yelü Hou
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Wuzhi; Yelü Hou

translations.literal: 〈 (opening parenthesis marking an alternate name)

sentences.zh: （何魯不）〉

translations.literal: (Helubu)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Helubu)〉

sentences.zh: 耶律安摶耶律窪耶律頹昱耶律撻烈

translations.literal: Yelü Antuan, Yelü Wa, Yelü Tuiyu, Yelü Talie
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Antuan; Yelü Wa; Yelü Tuiyu; Yelü Talie

sentences.zh: 耶律屋質，字敵輦，系出孟父房。

translations.literal: Yelü Wuzhi, style name Dirin, traced his descent to the Mengfu House branch.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Wuzhi, whose style name was Dirin, came from the Mengfu House branch.

sentences.zh: 姿簡靜，有器識，重然諾。

translations.literal: In bearing he was simple and still; he possessed discernment and held promises in weighty regard.
translations.idiomatic: He was quiet and unassuming in manner, shrewd and far-seeing, and deeply honored his word.

sentences.zh: 遇事造次，處之從容，人莫能測。

translations.literal: When affairs came upon him abruptly, he handled them with composure, so that no one could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Even when events struck suddenly, he met them with calm poise, and none could read his mind.

sentences.zh: 博學，知天文。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, he understood astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely learned and versed in astronomy.

sentences.zh: 會同間，為惕隱。

translations.literal: During the Tonghe era, he served as Tiyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tonghe period he held the office of Tiyin.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，諸大臣立世宗，太后聞之，怒甚，遣皇子李胡以兵逆擊，遇安端、劉哥等於泰德泉，敗歸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong died, the chief ministers enthroned Emperor Shizong. When the Empress Dowager heard of it, she was extremely angry and sent Prince Li Hu with troops to strike in counterattack. At Taide Spring he encountered Anduan, Liuge, and others, was defeated, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's death the great ministers enthroned Shizong. The Empress Dowager, enraged at the news, sent her son Li Hu at the head of an army to oppose them. Li Hu met Anduan, Liuge, and others at Taide Spring, was defeated, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 李胡盡執世宗臣僚家屬，謂守者曰：「我戰不克，先殪此曹！

translations.literal: Li Hu seized all the families of Shizong's ministers and officials and told the guards: "If I do not win the battle, I will slaughter these people first!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Hu arrested the households of Shizong's officials and ministers and told the guards, "If I cannot win the fight, I will kill every one of these people first!"

sentences.zh: 」人皆恟渙相謂曰：「若果戰，則是父子兄弟相夷矣！

translations.literal: " Everyone panicked and said to one another: "If we really fight, then fathers and sons and brothers will destroy one another!"
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were thrown into uproar, muttering among themselves, "If it comes to battle, fathers, sons, and brothers will cut one another down!"

sentences.zh: 」軍次潢河橫渡，隔岸相拒。

translations.literal: " The army halted at the Huang River ford; the two sides faced each other across the water.
translations.idiomatic: The armies halted at the Huang River crossing and confronted each other from opposite banks.

sentences.zh: 時屋質從太后，世宗以屋質善籌，欲行間，乃設事奉書，以試太后。

translations.literal: At that time Wuzhi was with the Empress Dowager. Shizong, knowing Wuzhi was skilled in strategy, wished to sow discord and therefore devised a pretext to submit a letter, testing the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi was then serving the Empress Dowager. Shizong, knowing his gift for strategy, tried to drive a wedge between them and sent a letter on a fabricated pretext to test her.

sentences.zh: 太后得書，以示屋質。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager received the letter and showed it to Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When the letter arrived she showed it to Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 屋質讀竟，言曰：「太后佐太祖定天下，故臣願竭死力。

translations.literal: When Wuzhi had finished reading, he said: "The Empress Dowager assisted Emperor Taizu in settling the empire; therefore your subject is willing to exhaust his strength unto death.
translations.idiomatic: After reading it through he said, "Your Majesty aided Taizu in pacifying the realm; this subject would gladly die in your service.

sentences.zh: 若太后見疑，臣雖欲盡忠，得乎？

translations.literal: If the Empress Dowager suspects me, though I wish to give full loyalty, may I do so?
translations.idiomatic: But if you doubt me, how can I prove my loyalty?

sentences.zh: 為今之計，莫若以言和解，事必有成；

translations.literal: For the plan of the moment, nothing surpasses reconciling by words—success is certain;
translations.idiomatic: The best course now is to settle matters by negotiation—talk will succeed;

sentences.zh: 否即宜速戰，以決勝負。

translations.literal: if not, we should fight swiftly to decide victory or defeat.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise fight at once and let fortune decide.

sentences.zh: 然人心一搖，國禍不淺，惟太后裁察。

translations.literal: Yet once hearts waver, national disaster will not be shallow—only the Empress Dowager may judge."
translations.idiomatic: Yet if hearts waver the realm itself is at risk—only Your Majesty can judge."

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「我若疑卿，安肯以書示汝？

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "If I suspected you, how would I be willing to show you the letter?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "If I mistrusted you, would I have shown you the letter?"

sentences.zh: 」屋質對曰：「李胡、永康王皆太祖子孫，神器非移他族，何不可之有？

translations.literal: Wuzhi replied: "Li Hu and the Prince of Yongkang are both descendants of Emperor Taizu; the imperial regalia does not pass to another clan—what could not be permitted?
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi answered, "Li Hu and the Prince of Yongkang are both Taizu's descendants; the throne does not pass outside the clan—what objection can there be?

sentences.zh: 太后宜思長策，與永康王和議。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager should consider a long-term plan and negotiate peace with the Prince of Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should think of a lasting policy and seek reconciliation with the Prince of Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「誰可遣者？

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager said: "Who can be sent?"
translations.idiomatic: She asked, "Whom can we send?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「太后不疑臣，臣請往。

translations.literal: He replied: "If the Empress Dowager does not suspect your subject, your subject requests to go.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "If Your Majesty does not doubt me, I beg to go myself.

sentences.zh: 萬一永康王見聽，廟社之福。

translations.literal: If by chance the Prince of Yongkang heeds us, it will be a blessing to the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: If the prince should listen, it will be fortune for the realm."

sentences.zh: 」太后乃遣屋質授書於帝。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then sent Wuzhi to deliver the letter to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager then dispatched Wuzhi to present the letter to Shizong.

sentences.zh: 帝遣宣徽使耶律海思復書，辭多不遜。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Yelü Haisi to reply; the wording was largely insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent the palace commissioner Yelü Haisi to answer, and the reply was for the most part defiant.

sentences.zh: 屋質諫曰：「書意如此，國家之憂未艾也。

translations.literal: Wuzhi remonstrated: "With the letter's meaning thus, the state's troubles are not yet ended.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi urged him, "With a reply like this, the realm's troubles are far from over.

sentences.zh: 能釋怨以安社稷，則臣以為莫若和好。

translations.literal: If we can release resentment to settle the altars of state, then your subject believes nothing surpasses making peace."
translations.idiomatic: If we can lay aside grievance to secure the altars of state, I see no better course than reconciliation."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「彼眾烏合，安能敵我？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Their host is a mob gathered in haste—how can they match us?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Their force is a rabble—how can it stand against us?"

sentences.zh: 」屋質曰：「即不敵，奈骨肉何！

translations.literal: Wuzhi said: "Even if they do not match us, what of flesh and blood!"
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi said, "Even if they cannot match us, what of kinship?!"

sentences.zh: 況未知孰勝。

translations.literal: Moreover, it is not yet known which side will prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, no one yet knows who would win.

sentences.zh: 借曰幸勝，諸臣之族執於李胡者，無噍類矣。

translations.literal: Suppose by chance we win—the clans of the ministers held by Li Hu would leave not a mouthful alive.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose we did win: the families of your ministers held by Li Hu would be wiped out to the last mouth.

sentences.zh: 以此計之，惟和為善。

translations.literal: Weighing it thus, only peace is good."
translations.idiomatic: Weighing the matter, peace alone is wise."

sentences.zh: 」左右聞者失色。

translations.literal: Those at his side who heard turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard him at the emperor's side went pale.

sentences.zh: 帝良久，問曰：「若何而和？

translations.literal: After a long silence the Emperor asked: "How then shall we make peace?"
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence the emperor asked, "How then can we make peace?"

sentences.zh: 」屋質對曰：「與太后相見，各紓忿恚，和之不難；

translations.literal: Wuzhi replied: "Meet the Empress Dowager face to face, each easing wrath and resentment—peace will not be hard;
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi answered, "Meet the Empress Dowager in person, each laying aside anger, and peace will not be hard;

sentences.zh: 不然，決戰非晚。

translations.literal: if not, decisive battle is not late."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise decisive battle is still an option."

sentences.zh: 」帝然之，遂遣海思詣太后約和。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved and thereupon sent Haisi to the Empress Dowager to arrange peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent Haisi to the empress dowager to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 往返數日，議乃定。

translations.literal: After several days of going back and forth, the terms were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Messengers shuttled for several days until terms were fixed.

sentences.zh: 始相見，怨言交讓，殊無和意。

translations.literal: At their first meeting, grievances were exchanged in mutual reproach; there was utterly no intent to reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: At the first meeting they traded grievances and reproaches, with no sign of reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 太后謂屋質曰：「汝當為我畫之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said to Wuzhi: "You must devise a plan for me."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager told Wuzhi, "You must find a way for me."

sentences.zh: 」屋質進曰：「太后與大王若能釋怨，臣乃敢進說。

translations.literal: Wuzhi advanced and said: "If the Empress Dowager and the Great King can release resentment, your subject then dares to offer counsel."
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi stepped forward and said, "If Your Majesty and the Great King can lay aside grievance, only then dare I speak."

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「汝第言之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "Speak on."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Speak plainly."

sentences.zh: 」屋質借謁者籌執之，謂太后曰：「昔人皇王在，何故立嗣聖？

translations.literal: Wuzhi borrowed counting rods from an attendant and, holding them, said to the Empress Dowager: "In former days when the Renhuang King was present, why was Emperor Sishèng enthroned?"
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi took counting rods from an attendant and, holding them, asked the Empress Dowager, "When the Renhuang King was still alive, why was Sishèng made emperor?"

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「立嗣聖者，太祖遺旨。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "Enthroning Sishèng was Emperor Taizu's final command."
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "Sishèng's enthronement was Taizu's dying wish."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「大王何故擅立，不稟尊親？

translations.literal: He said again: "Why did the Great King presume to enthrone himself without reporting to his honored kin?"
translations.idiomatic: He went on, "Why did the Great King enthrone himself on his own authority, without consulting his elders?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「人皇王當立而不立，所以去之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Renhuang King ought to have been enthroned but was not—therefore he was removed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Renhuang King should have been enthroned but was not—that is why he was set aside."

sentences.zh: 」屋質正色曰：「人皇王舍父母之國而奔唐，子道當如是耶？

translations.literal: Wuzhi said with stern countenance: "The Renhuang King abandoned his parents' state and fled to Tang—should a son's conduct be thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi said sternly, "The Renhuang King abandoned his parents' realm and fled to Tang—is that how a son should behave?"

sentences.zh: 大王見太后，不少遜謝，惟怨是尋。

translations.literal: The Great King, on meeting the Empress Dowager, offered little deference or apology and sought only grievance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great King met the empress dowager he showed little deference or apology and nursed only grievance.

sentences.zh: 太后牽於偏愛，托先帝遺命，妄授神器。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager, constrained by partial affection, invoked the late emperor's testament and rashly bestowed the regalia of state.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager, swayed by partial love, invoked the late emperor's testament and rashly handed over the throne.

sentences.zh: 如此何敢望和，當速交戰！

translations.literal: With matters thus, how dare we hope for peace—we should fight at once!"
translations.idiomatic: With matters thus, how can we hope for peace? We should fight at once!"

sentences.zh: 」擲籌而退。

translations.literal: He cast down the rods and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He threw down the rods and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太后泣曰：「向太祖遭諸弟亂，天下荼毒，瘡痍未復，庸可再乎！

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wept and said: "Formerly when Emperor Taizu suffered turmoil from his younger brothers, the realm was ravaged and wounds were not yet healed—how could it happen again!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wept and said, "When Taizu was torn by his brothers' rebellion the realm was ravaged and the wounds are not yet healed—can we endure it again?!"

sentences.zh: 」乃索籌一。

translations.literal: She then asked for one counting rod.
translations.idiomatic: She asked for a counting rod.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「父不為而子為，又誰咎也！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What the father did not do the son will do—whom else shall we blame!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What the father would not do the son will do—whom else is there to blame?!"

sentences.zh: 」亦取籌而執。

translations.literal: He too took a rod and held it.
translations.idiomatic: He too took a rod and held it.

sentences.zh: 左右感激，大慟。

translations.literal: Those at their sides were deeply moved and wept loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Those standing by were deeply moved and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 太后復謂屋質曰：「議既定，神器竟誰歸？

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager again said to Wuzhi: "Now that the terms are settled, to whom in the end shall the regalia of state pass?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager again asked Wuzhi, "Now that terms are settled, to whom shall the throne pass?"

sentences.zh: 」屋質曰：「太后若授永康王，順天合人，復何疑？

translations.literal: Wuzhi said: "If the Empress Dowager invests the Prince of Yongkang, it accords with Heaven and with men—what further doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi said, "If Your Majesty invests the Prince of Yongkang, it accords with Heaven and with the people—what further doubt?"

sentences.zh: 」李胡厲聲曰：「我在，兀欲安得立！

translations.literal: Li Hu said in a harsh voice: "While I am alive, how can Wuyu be enthroned!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Hu cried out, "While I live, how can Wuyu be enthroned?!"

sentences.zh: 」屋質曰：「禮有世嫡，不傳諸弟。

translations.literal: Wuzhi said: "Rites provide for succession by the heir of the generation; it is not passed to younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi said, "Rites provide that succession passes to the heir of the generation, not to younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 昔嗣聖之立，尚以為非，況公暴戾殘忍，人多怨讟。

translations.literal: Formerly Sishèng's enthronement was still held wrong; how much more you, violent and cruel, with many men resenting and reviling you.
translations.idiomatic: Even Sishèng's enthronement was widely judged wrong; how much more you, violent and cruel, with the people full of resentment.

sentences.zh: 萬口一辭，願立永康王，不可奪也。

translations.literal: Ten thousand mouths speak as one, wishing to enthrone the Prince of Yongkang—it cannot be taken away."
translations.idiomatic: Every voice as one calls for the Prince of Yongkang—the wish cannot be denied."

sentences.zh: 」太后顧李胡曰：「汝亦聞此言乎？

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager turned to Li Hu and said: "Have you also heard these words?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager turned to Li Hu and said, "Have you heard this too?"

sentences.zh: 汝實自為之！

translations.literal: You have brought it on yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: You brought this on yourself!"

sentences.zh: 」乃許立永康。

translations.literal: She then agreed to enthrone Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: She then agreed to enthrone the Prince of Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 帝謂屋質曰：「汝與朕屬尤近，何反助太后？

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Wuzhi: "You and I are especially close in kin—why did you instead aid the Empress Dowager?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Wuzhi, "You and I are especially close in kin—why did you side with the empress dowager?"

sentences.zh: 」屋質對曰：「臣以社稷至重，不可輕付，故如是耳。

translations.literal: Wuzhi replied: "Your subject holds the altars of state supremely weighty and not to be lightly entrusted—therefore it was thus."
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi answered, "I hold the realm too weighty to entrust lightly—that is why I acted as I did."

sentences.zh: 」上喜其忠。

translations.literal: The sovereign was pleased at his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased with his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 天祿二年，耶律天德、蕭翰謀反下獄，惕隱劉哥及其弟盆都結天德等為亂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianlu, Yelü Tiande and Xiao Han plotted rebellion and were imprisoned; the Tiyin Liuge and his younger brother Pendu joined Tiande and others in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianlu, Yelü Tiande and Xiao Han were imprisoned for plotting rebellion; the Tiyin Liuge and his brother Pendu joined Tiande and others in a conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 耶律石剌潛告屋質，屋質遽引入見，白其事。

translations.literal: Yelü Shila secretly informed Wuzhi; Wuzhi hurried to bring him in to an audience and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Shila secretly informed Wuzhi, who at once brought him before the emperor and reported the plot.

sentences.zh: 劉哥等不服，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Liuge and the others would not confess; the matter then lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Liuge and his party denied the charge, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 未幾，劉哥邀駕觀樗蒲，捧觴上壽，袖刃而進。

translations.literal: Before long, Liuge invited the emperor to watch chestnut-horse racing, raised a cup to offer longevity, and advanced with a blade hidden in his sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liuge invited the emperor to watch a dice game, raised a cup in toast, and advanced with a blade hidden in his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 帝覺，命執之，親詰其事。

translations.literal: The emperor perceived it, ordered him seized, and personally interrogated the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sensed it, had him seized, and questioned him in person.

sentences.zh: 劉哥自誓，帝復不問。

translations.literal: Liuge swore oaths on himself; the emperor again did not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: Liuge swore his innocence, and the emperor again let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 屋質奏曰：「當使劉哥與石剌對狀，不可輒恕。

translations.literal: Wuzhi memorialized: "Liuge should be made to confront Shila in testimony; he must not be lightly pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi urged, "Liuge must confront Shila in testimony—you must not forgive this lightly."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿為朕鞫之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You shall investigate for Us."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Investigate it for me."

sentences.zh: 」屋質率劍士往訊之，天德等伏罪。

translations.literal: Wuzhi led swordsmen to interrogate them; Tiande and the others confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi led swordsmen to question them, and Tiande and the others confessed.

sentences.zh: 誅天德，杖翰，遷劉哥，以盆都使轄戛斯國。

translations.literal: Tiande was executed, Han was flogged, Liuge was transferred, and Pendu was sent as envoy to the Kirghiz.
translations.idiomatic: Tiande was executed, Han was flogged, Liuge was banished, and Pendu was sent as envoy to the Kirghiz.

sentences.zh: 三年，表列泰寧王察割陰謀事，上不聽。

translations.literal: In the third year he memorialized listing the Prince of Taining Chagai's secret plots; the sovereign did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he reported the Prince of Taining Chagai's secret conspiracy; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 五年，為右皮室詳穩。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he became Right Pishi Xiangwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Right Pishi Xiangwen.

sentences.zh: 秋，上祭讓國皇帝於行宮，與群臣皆醉，察割弒帝。

translations.literal: In autumn the sovereign sacrificed to the Emperor Who Yielded the State at the traveling palace; he and the chief ministers were all drunk, and Chagai assassinated the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the emperor sacrificed to the Yielding-State Emperor at the traveling palace; he and his ministers were all drunk when Chagai murdered him.

sentences.zh: 屋質聞有言「衣紫者不可失」，乃易衣而出，亟遣人召諸王，乃喻禁衛長皮室等同力討賊。

translations.literal: Wuzhi heard a saying that "whoever wears purple must not be lost"; he therefore changed clothes and went out, urgently sent men to summon the princes, and instructed the commander of the guard Pishi and others to join forces against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi heard someone say, "Whoever wears purple must not be lost"; he changed clothes and went out, urgently summoned the princes, and urged the guard commander Pishi and others to join in suppressing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時壽安王歸帳，屋質遣弟沖迎之。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Shou'an returned to camp; Wuzhi sent his younger brother Chong to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shou'an had just returned to camp; Wuzhi sent his younger brother Chong to meet him.

sentences.zh: 王至，尚猶豫。

translations.literal: When the prince arrived, he still hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince arrived he still hesitated.

sentences.zh: 屋質曰：「大王嗣聖子，賊若得之，必不容。

translations.literal: Wuzhi said: "Great King, you are Sishèng's son; if the rebels obtain you, they will certainly not spare you.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi said, "Great King, you are Sishèng's son; if the rebels seize you they will not spare you.

sentences.zh: 群臣將誰事，社稷將誰賴？

translations.literal: To whom will the chief ministers turn in service, on whom will the altars of state rely?
translations.idiomatic: Whom will the ministers serve, on whom will the realm rely?

sentences.zh: 萬一落賊手，悔將何及？

translations.literal: If by chance you fall into the rebels' hands, what regret will suffice?"
translations.idiomatic: If you fall into rebel hands, what regret will be enough?"

sentences.zh: 」王始悟。

translations.literal: The prince then understood.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then understood.

sentences.zh: 諸將聞屋質出，相繼而至。

translations.literal: When the generals heard Wuzhi had come out, they arrived one after another.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals heard Wuzhi had emerged, they gathered one after another.

sentences.zh: 遲明整兵，出賊不意，圍之，遂誅察割。

translations.literal: At daybreak they arrayed the troops, took the rebels unawares, surrounded them, and thereupon executed Chagai.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak they formed ranks, caught the rebels off guard, surrounded them, and executed Chagai.

sentences.zh: 亂既平，穆宗即位，謂屋質曰：「朕之性命，實出卿手。

translations.literal: When the turmoil was settled, Emperor Muzong took the throne and said to Wuzhi: "Our life in truth came from your hand.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored Muzong took the throne and told Wuzhi, "My life was truly in your hands.

sentences.zh: 」命知國事，以逆黨財產盡賜之，屋質固辭。

translations.literal: " He ordered him to oversee state affairs and bestowed on him all the rebel party's property in full; Wuzhi firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He put him in charge of state affairs and offered him all the rebels' property; Wuzhi firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 應歷五年，為北院大王，總山西事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yingli he became North Great King and oversaw all Shanxi affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yingli he became North Great King with overall charge of the Shanxi region.

sentences.zh: 耶律吼，字曷魯，六院部夷離堇蒲古只之後。

translations.literal: Yelü Hou, style name Helu, was a descendant of Pugu Zhi, yilizhen of the Six Yuan Divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Hou, whose style name was Helu, descended from Pugu Zhi, yilizhen of the Six Yuan Divisions.

sentences.zh: 端愨好施，不事生產。

translations.literal: Upright and sincere, he delighted in giving and did not engage in production.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and generous, and did not trouble himself with acquiring wealth.

sentences.zh: 太宗特加倚任。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong especially added trust in him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong placed special trust in him.

sentences.zh: 會同六年，為南院大王，蒞事清簡，人不敢以年少易之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tonghe he became South Great King; his conduct of affairs was clear and simple, and men did not dare treat him lightly because of his youth.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tonghe he became South Great King; his administration was clear and spare, and none dared slight him for his youth.

sentences.zh: 時晉主石重貴表不稱臣，辭多踞慢，吼言晉罪不可不伐。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin ruler Shi Chonggui in his memorial did not style himself subject; the wording was largely arrogant and insolent. Hou said the Jin crime could not go unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Jin ruler Shi Chonggui sent a memorial refusing to style himself a subject, with language arrogant and insolent, Hou urged that Jin's offense could not go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 及帝親征，以所部兵從。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned in person, he followed with the troops under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned in person, Hou followed with his own troops.

sentences.zh: 既入汴，諸將皆取內帑珍異，吼獨取馬鎧，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: After entering Bian, all the generals took rare treasures from the inner treasury; Hou alone took horse armor, and the emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: After the army entered Bian, the other generals looted rare treasures from the inner treasury; Hou took only horse armor, and the emperor praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩於欒城，無遺詔，軍中憂懼不知所為。

translations.literal: When the emperor died at Luancheng there was no testament; the army was anxious and fearful, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died at Luancheng without leaving a testament, the army was gripped by fear and uncertainty.

sentences.zh: 吼詣北院大王耶律窪議曰：「天位不可一日曠。

translations.literal: Hou went to the North Great King Yelü Wa to discuss and said: "The throne cannot stand vacant for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Hou went to the North Great King Yelü Wa and said, "The throne cannot stand empty for even a day.

sentences.zh: 若請於太后，則必屬李胡。

translations.literal: If we ask the Empress Dowager, it will certainly fall to Li Hu.
translations.idiomatic: If we appeal to the empress dowager, the succession will certainly go to Li Hu.

sentences.zh: 李胡暴戾殘忍，詎能子民。

translations.literal: Li Hu is violent and cruel—how could he be a father to the people?
translations.idiomatic: Li Hu is violent and cruel—how could he rule as a true sovereign?

sentences.zh: 必欲厭人望。

translations.literal: If we must satisfy the people's hopes,
translations.idiomatic: If we mean to satisfy what the people hope for,

sentences.zh: 則當立永康王。

translations.literal: then we should enthrone the Prince of Yongkang."
translations.idiomatic: we must enthrone the Prince of Yongkang."

sentences.zh: 」窪然之。

translations.literal: Wa approved.
translations.idiomatic: Wa agreed.

sentences.zh: 會耶律安摶來，意與吼合，遂定議立永康王，是為世宗。

translations.literal: When Yelü Antuan came, his intent matched Hou's; they thereupon fixed the decision to enthrone the Prince of Yongkang, who became Emperor Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yelü Antuan arrived his views matched Hou's; they settled on enthroning the Prince of Yongkang, who became Emperor Shizong.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以功加采訪使，賜以寶貨。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, for his merit he was made Commissioner of Investigation and bestowed treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Commissioner of Investigation for his service and rewarded with precious goods.

sentences.zh: 吼辭曰：「臣位已高，敢復求富！

translations.literal: Hou declined, saying: "Your subject's rank is already high—how dare he seek wealth again!
translations.idiomatic: Hou declined, saying, "My rank is already high—how dare I seek more wealth!"

sentences.zh: 臣從弟的錄諸子坐事籍沒，陛下哀而出之，則臣受賜多矣。

translations.literal: Your subject's younger cousin Di Lu's sons were implicated in a case and their property confiscated; if Your Majesty in pity releases them, your subject will have received ample favor."
translations.idiomatic: My cousin Di Lu's sons were implicated in a case and their property was confiscated; if Your Majesty releases them in mercy, I will have received more than enough."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「吼舍重賞，以族人為請，其賢遠甚。

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "Hou abandons heavy reward and pleads for his clansmen—his worthiness far surpasses others."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Hou forgoes rich reward to plead for his kin—his virtue far surpasses the common run."

sentences.zh: 」許之，仍賜宮戶五十。

translations.literal: He granted it and still bestowed fifty palace households.
translations.idiomatic: He granted the request and still gave him fifty palace households.

sentences.zh: 時有取當世名流作《七賢傳》者，吼與其一。

translations.literal: At the time someone compiled eminent men of the age into a Biographies of the Seven Worthies; Hou was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When someone compiled a Biographies of the Seven Worthies from the leading men of the day, Hou was counted among them.

sentences.zh: 天祿三年卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Tianlu, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Tianlu at the age of thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子何魯不。

translations.literal: His son was Helubu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Helubu.

sentences.zh: 耶律安摶，曾祖巖木，玄祖之長子。

translations.literal: Yelü Antuan—his great-grandfather was Yanmu, eldest son of the Xuan Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Antuan's great-grandfather Yanmu was the eldest son of the Xuan Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 祖楚不魯，為本部夷離堇。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chubulu served as yilizhen of the tribal division.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chubulu was yilizhen of their division.

sentences.zh: 父叠裏，幼多疾，時太祖為撻馬狘沙裏，常加撫育。

translations.literal: His father Dieli, sickly from youth, was often nurtured by the Taizu of that time when he was tamo yashali.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dieli had been frail since childhood; when Taizu was still tamo yashali he often cared for the boy.

sentences.zh: 神冊六年，為惕隱，從太祖將龍軍討阻卜、党項有功。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shence he became Tiyin; following Taizu he led the Dragon Army against the Zubu and Tangut with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shence he became Tiyin and followed Taizu in leading the Dragon Army against the Zubu and Tangut with distinction.

sentences.zh: 天贊三年，為南院夷離堇，征渤海，攻忽汗城，俘斬甚眾。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianzan he became South Yuan yilizhen; campaigning against Bohai he attacked Hohan city and captured and slew a great host.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianzan he became South Yuan yilizhen; in the campaign against Bohai he attacked Hohan city and took or killed a great number of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，淳欽皇后稱制，欲以大元帥嗣位。

translations.literal: When Taizu died, Empress Chunqin assumed regency and wished the Great Marshal to succeed to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu's death Empress Chunqin ruled as regent and wished to enthrone the Great Marshal as successor.

sentences.zh: 叠裏建言，帝位宣先嫡長；

translations.literal: Dieli offered counsel that the imperial seat should go first to the eldest son of the principal wife;
translations.idiomatic: Dieli urged that the throne should pass first to the eldest son of the principal wife;

sentences.zh: 今東丹王赴朝，當立。

translations.literal: now the Prince of Dongdan has come to court and ought to be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Dongdan has now come to court and ought to be enthroned.

sentences.zh: 由是忤旨。

translations.literal: For this he offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: For this he offended the throne.

sentences.zh: 以黨附東丹王，詔下獄，訊鞫，加以炮烙。

translations.literal: On the charge of siding with the Prince of Dongdan, an edict sent him to prison; he was interrogated and subjected to roasting torture.
translations.idiomatic: Accused of siding with the Prince of Dongdan, he was imprisoned, interrogated, and tortured with fire.

sentences.zh: 不伏，殺之，籍其家。

translations.literal: He would not confess; they killed him and confiscated his household.
translations.idiomatic: He would not confess; he was executed and his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 安摶自幼若成人，居父喪，哀毀過禮，見者傷之。

translations.literal: Antuan from childhood was like an adult; in mourning for his father his grief exceeded the rites, and those who saw it were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Antuan had been grave beyond his years since childhood; in mourning his father he grieved beyond the rites, and all who saw him were moved.

sentences.zh: 太宗屢加慰諭，嘗曰：「此兒必為令器。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong repeatedly comforted and instructed him, once saying: "This boy will surely be an outstanding vessel."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong often comforted him and once said, "This boy will surely prove a fine instrument of state."

sentences.zh: 」既長，寡言笑，重然諾，動遵繩矩，事母至孝。

translations.literal: When grown he spoke and laughed little, held promises in weight, in conduct followed the measuring cord, and in serving his mother was supremely filial.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he was sparing of speech and laughter, deeply honored his word, kept strictly to rule, and served his mother with utmost filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 以父死非罪，未葬，不預宴樂。

translations.literal: Because his father died without guilt and was not yet buried, he did not take part in feasts or music.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had died unjustly and was not yet buried, he refused feasts and music.

sentences.zh: 世宗在藩邸，尤加憐恤，安摶密自結納。

translations.literal: When Shizong was at the princely residence, he especially showed pity and care; Antuan secretly attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: While Shizong was still at his princely residence Antuan showed him special regard and secretly attached himself to him.

sentences.zh: 太宗伐晉還，至欒城崩，諸將欲立世宗，以李胡及壽安王在朝，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Taizong campaigned against Jin and on the return died at Luancheng; the generals wished to enthrone Shizong, but because Li Hu and the Prince of Shou'an were at court they hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong died at Luancheng on the return from campaigning against Jin; the generals wished to enthrone Shizong, but with Li Hu and the Prince of Shou'an still at court they hesitated.

sentences.zh: 時安摶直宿衛，世宗密召問計。

translations.literal: At that time Antuan was on palace guard duty; Shizong secretly summoned him to ask his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Antuan was then on palace guard duty; Shizong secretly summoned him for counsel.

sentences.zh: 安摶曰：「大王聰安寬恕，人皇王之嫡長；

translations.literal: Antuan said: "Great King, you are intelligent, peaceful, and forgiving—the Renhuang King's eldest son of the principal wife;
translations.idiomatic: Antuan said, "Great King, you are intelligent, calm, and magnanimous—the Renhuang King's eldest son by the principal wife;

sentences.zh: 先帝雖有壽安，天下屬意多在大王。

translations.literal: though the late emperor had Shou'an, the realm's hopes lie mostly with the Great King.
translations.idiomatic: though the late emperor also had Shou'an, the realm's hopes rest chiefly on you.

sentences.zh: 今若不斷，後悔無及。

translations.literal: If you do not decide now, regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not act now, regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 」會有自京師來者，安摶詐以李胡死傳報軍中，皆以為信。

translations.literal: It happened that someone came from the capital; Antuan falsely spread word in the army that Li Hu was dead, and all believed it.
translations.idiomatic: When someone arrived from the capital Antuan falsely reported in camp that Li Hu was dead, and all believed it.

sentences.zh: 於是安摶詣北、南二大王計之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Antuan went to the North and South Great Kings to consult.
translations.idiomatic: Antuan then went to consult the North and South Great Kings.

sentences.zh: 北院大王窪聞而遽起曰：「吾二人方議此事。

translations.literal: The North Great King Wa, hearing, rose hastily and said: "We two were just discussing this matter.
translations.idiomatic: The North Great King Wa, hearing this, rose at once and said, "We two were just discussing this very matter.

sentences.zh: 先帝嘗欲以永康王為儲貳，今日之事，有我輩在，孰敢不從！

translations.literal: The late emperor once wished to make the Prince of Yongkang heir apparent; in today's affair, with us here, who would dare not follow!
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor once meant to make the Prince of Yongkang heir; with us here today, who would dare refuse!"

sentences.zh: 但恐不白太后而立，為國家啟釁。

translations.literal: Yet I fear that enthroning without informing the Empress Dowager will open strife for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear enthroning him without informing the empress dowager may open strife for the realm."

sentences.zh: 」安摶對曰：「大王既知先帝欲以永康王為儲副，況永康王賢明，人心樂附。

translations.literal: Antuan replied: "Great King, you already know the late emperor wished to make the Prince of Yongkang heir; moreover the Prince of Yongkang is worthy and wise, and men's hearts gladly attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Antuan answered, "You already know the late emperor wished to make the Prince of Yongkang heir; he is worthy and wise, and the people gladly follow him.

sentences.zh: 今天下甫定，稍緩則大事去矣。

translations.literal: The realm has just been settled; if we delay even slightly the great affair will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has only just been settled; the slightest delay and the chance is gone.

sentences.zh: 若白太后，必立李胡。

translations.literal: If we inform the Empress Dowager, she will certainly enthrone Li Hu.
translations.idiomatic: If we inform the empress dowager she will certainly enthrone Li Hu.

sentences.zh: 且李胡殘暴，行路共知，果嗣位，如社稷何？

translations.literal: Moreover Li Hu is brutal—travelers on the road all know it; if he truly succeeds, what of the altars of state?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Hu is brutal—every traveler knows it; if he truly succeeds, what becomes of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 」南院大王吼曰：「此言是也。

translations.literal: The South Great King Hou said: "These words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: The South Great King Hou said, "He is right.

sentences.zh: 吾計決矣！

translations.literal: My plan is settled!"
translations.idiomatic: My mind is made up!"

sentences.zh: 」乃整軍，召諸將奉世宗即位於太宗柩前。

translations.literal: They thereupon arrayed the army, summoned the generals, and enthroned Shizong before Taizong's bier.
translations.idiomatic: They formed the ranks, summoned the generals, and enthroned Shizong before Taizong's bier.

sentences.zh: 帝立，以安摶為腹心，總知宿衛。

translations.literal: When the emperor was established, he made Antuan his intimate and put him in overall charge of palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, the emperor made Antuan his closest confidant and put him in charge of palace security.

sentences.zh: 是歲，約和於潢河橫渡。

translations.literal: That year peace was arranged at the Huang River ford.
translations.idiomatic: That year peace was concluded at the Huang River crossing.

sentences.zh: 太后問安摶曰：「吾與汝有何隙？

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager asked Antuan: "What grievance lies between you and me?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager asked Antuan, "What grievance lies between us?"

sentences.zh: 」安摶以父死為對，太后默然。

translations.literal: Antuan answered with his father's death; the Empress Dowager was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Antuan answered with his father's unjust death; the empress dowager fell silent.

sentences.zh: 及置北院樞密使，上命安摶為之，賜奴婢百口，寵任無比，事皆取決焉。

translations.literal: When the North Yuan Commissioner of Military Affairs was established, the sovereign appointed Antuan to it, bestowed a hundred male and female servants, favored and entrusted him beyond compare, and all affairs were decided by him.
translations.idiomatic: When the North Yuan Commissioner of Military Affairs was created the emperor appointed Antuan to the post, gave him a hundred servants, favored him beyond any other, and left all decisions to him.

sentences.zh: 然性太寬，事循茍簡，豪猾縱恣不能制。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was too lenient; in affairs he followed lax simplicity and could not restrain the powerful and cunning who ran riot.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was too lenient by nature, careless and perfunctory in office, and unable to restrain powerful ruffians who ran riot.

sentences.zh: 天祿末，察割兵犯禦幄，又不能討，由是中外短之。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianlu, Chagai's troops violated the imperial quarters, and he could not suppress them; for this court and countryside faulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianlu, when Chagai's troops attacked the imperial quarters, he failed to suppress them, and court and country alike faulted him.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，以立世宗之故，不復委用。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, because of his role in enthroning Shizong, he was no longer entrusted with office.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, because Antuan had helped enthrone Shizong, he was no longer given office.

sentences.zh: 應歷三年，或誣安摶與齊王罨撒葛謀亂，系獄死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yingli someone falsely accused Antuan of plotting disorder with Prince Qi Yansage; he was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yingli he was falsely accused of plotting rebellion with Prince Qi Yansage, imprisoned, and died.

sentences.zh: 侄撒給，左皮室詳穩。

translations.literal: His nephew Sagie was Left Pishi Xiangwen.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Sagie served as Left Pishi Xiangwen.

sentences.zh: 撻烈凡用兵，賞罰信明，得士卒心。

translations.literal: In all his use of troops Talie made rewards and punishments faithful and clear, winning the hearts of officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In all his campaigns Talie made rewards and punishments clear and sure, and won the soldiers' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 河東單弱，不為周、宋所並者，撻烈有力焉。

translations.literal: Hedong was isolated and weak; that it was not swallowed by Zhou and Song owed much to Talie's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong stood isolated and weak; that Zhou and Song did not swallow it owed much to Talie's efforts.

sentences.zh: 在治所不修邊幅，百姓無稱，年谷屢稔。

translations.literal: At his seat of government he did not trim his appearance; the common people had no praise for show, yet harvests were repeatedly abundant.
translations.idiomatic: At his seat of government he cared nothing for appearances; the people had no grand praise for him, yet harvests were repeatedly abundant.

sentences.zh: 時耶律屋質居北院，撻烈居南院，俱有政跡，朝議以為「富民大王」云。

translations.literal: At that time Yelü Wuzhi held the North Yuan and Talie the South Yuan; both had administrative achievements, and court opinion called them the "Great Kings Who Enrich the People."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yelü Wuzhi held the North Yuan and Talie the South Yuan; both governed well, and the court called them the "Great Kings Who Enrich the People."

sentences.zh: 贊曰：立嗣以嫡，禮也。

translations.literal: The encomium says: To establish succession by the principal heir is ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Establishing succession through the principal heir is ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，非安摶、吼、窪謀而克斷，策立世宗，非屋質直而能諫，杜太后之私，折李胡之暴，以成橫渡之約，則亂將誰定？

translations.literal: When Taizong died, had Antuan, Hou, and Wa not counseled and been able to decide and plan to enthrone Shizong; had Wuzhi not been upright and able to remonstrate, blocking the Empress Dowager's partiality and breaking Li Hu's violence to complete the agreement at the ford—who would have settled the turmoil?
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died, without Antuan, Hou, and Wa to counsel decisively and enthrone Shizong; without Wuzhi's upright remonstrance that checked the empress dowager's partiality, broke Li Hu's violence, and secured peace at the river crossing—who would have ended the turmoil?

sentences.zh: 四臣者，庶幾《春秋》首止之功哉。

translations.literal: These four ministers approach the achievement of the first and last stanzas in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: These four ministers approach the achievement praised in the opening and closing stanzas of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
